name: mandelbrot_load_imbalance
task: This project renders the Mandelbrot set, split across multiple translation units: include/iteration_map.h + src/iteration_map.cpp (a row-major grid of per-pixel escape-iteration counts with a per-row work helper), include/mandelbrot.h + src/mandelbrot.cpp (the per-point iteration kernel plus serial and OpenMP-parallel image computation), include/render.h + src/render.cpp (ASCII rendering and an inside-fraction statistic), and src/main.cpp (the profiling entry point). compute_mandelbrot_parallel() in src/mandelbrot.cpp parallelizes the row loop with '#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)' and has two problems. First, the shared 'total' iteration counter is updated by every thread without a reduction or atomic, so updates are lost and the returned total differs from compute_mandelbrot_serial(). Second, rows through the middle of the set need many more iterations than rows near the top and bottom, so static block scheduling leaves one or two threads with most of the work while the others finish early; the test harness measures the work (iteration count) assigned to each thread through the optional 'row_owner' output and requires the busiest thread to carry less than 1.25x the mean (this balance check is skipped on machines with fewer than 4 hardware threads). Fix compute_mandelbrot_parallel() so the iteration map and the returned total are identical to the serial version and the rows are distributed in a load-balanced way (for example schedule(dynamic, chunk) or a cyclic schedule), keeping the row loop parallelized with OpenMP and keeping the row_owner reporting working (row_owner[r] must still be the id of the thread that computed row r). Do not change any function signature declared in include/mandelbrot.h or include/iteration_map.h.
notes: build_command compiles the profiling entry point at build/app (src/main.cpp -> iteration_map.cpp, mandelbrot.cpp, render.cpp). This binary must be built and then executed via run_command to drive DiscoPoP's instrumentation and produce its dynamic profiling output, including dynamic_dependencies, over the parallel row loop in compute_mandelbrot_parallel(). test_command builds and runs a separate correctness harness at build/run_tests (from tests/test_main.cpp); it is independent of the profiling binary and should not be used as the DiscoPoP execution target. Both binaries link the same iteration_map.cpp, mandelbrot.cpp, render.cpp object files, so no separate CMake/Meson/etc. configuration is required — plain 'make' is sufficient to build, run, and test.
